utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, let the registrar call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-00-39 & 40-PT, the Prosecutor versus Momcilo Krajisnik and Biljana Plavsic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We can now hear the appearances.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon, my learned friends from the Defence. My name is Mark Harmon. I will be representing the Prosecutor in these proceedings. Appearing with me is the Prosecutor, Madam Carla Del Ponte. Appearing at the location of the videolink is Mr. Alan Tieger.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Eugene O'Sullivan, appearing on behalf of Mrs. Plavsic. And with her on location is lead counsel Mr. Robert Pavich.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mrs. Plavsic, can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PLAVSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can hear you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: This is a hearing at the request of the accused to change her plea to the indictment. Mr. O'Sullivan, do you ask that count 3 be put again?

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, that is our request.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Thank you. Biljana Plavsic, count 3 of this indictment charges you with persecution on political, racial, and religious grounds, a crime against humanity, punishable under Articles 5(H) and 7(1) and 7(3) of the Statue of the Tribunal. Mrs. Plavsic, how do you plead to that count; guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, we can't hear the defendant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Could you please repeat it. The interpreters have had trouble hearing.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PLAVSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I plead guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: You plead guilty. The Rules of the Tribunal require that the Trial Chamber is satisfied that a plea of guilty has been made voluntarily, that it is informed and not equivocal, and that there is a sufficient factual basis for the crime and the participation of the accused in it. Mrs. Plavsic, in the plea agreement which we have read, you have signed a declaration that you entered into the agreement freely and voluntarily, understanding its terms, and having been advised by your lawyers. You have also signed a statement to the same effect in which is added that the plea is informed and unequivocal. Do you confirm that those declarations are correct?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PLAVSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We understand that the Prosecutor will withdraw or have dismissed the remaining counts at the time of sentencing. Would you confirm, Mr. Harmon, that that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: That is correct, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. The Trial Chamber is satisfied of all the matters set out in Rule 62 bis, finds that this is a voluntary and informed and unequivocal plea, is satisfied as to the factual basis, and therefore enters a finding of guilt on count 3. It remains for us to fix a date for the sentencing hearing. We have available some days in December. I say "available." There is a trial going on, but we could make a period of time available during that occasion. That would be in the week of the 16th -- Monday, the 16th of December. We have in mind certainly that day, and we'll hear any submissions that anybody may have to make in regard to the length of the hearing. Mr. Harmon, how long would the Prosecution require?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. President, counsel and I have conferred on this matter on a number of occasions and it is our conclusion that we would require that the total length of the hearing would require three days. So we would request that a hearing be permitted during the time period of -- from December the 16th through the end of the 18th of December.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Why three days, Mr. Harmon? How many witnesses do you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: At this point, given that this matter has just been public, we have not fixed a witness list but we anticipate we will have a number of witnesses to call before this hearing, and we will be submitting those lists in consultation with the Chamber. But to be on the safe side, Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. we believe three days would be a time that would be sufficient, given the magnitude of this case and the importance of this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Harmon, my view is that the Tribunal cannot at this time afford to spend three days on a sentence hearing. I would say at the most one full day and one session of the next day. This is a sentence hearing; it's not a trial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Bear in mind that much of the evidence can be given in written form, particularly as far as the Prosecution are concerned. That's the time we have in mind. Mr. O'Sullivan, how many witnesses have you in mind to call?

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Well, can I start by saying the three days of which Mr. Harmon speaks is three days in totality for both parties. It's in that context that we're talking about three days.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, I took that into account, but my comments still remain.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Well, I would make the following points: That since this matter has only become public today, we as well are about to begin contacting potential witnesses. And in our submission, we are dealing with a case involving a high-level political leader who has entered a plea of guilty, and both parties would like to make full representation in court through its witnesses, and we are dealing with a person who is at the highest level of political leadership. And I know that in other plea hearings regarding other people at much lower levels, guards, for instance, a day or two has been set aside. So in our submission three days, given the magnitude of this case and the importance to our client, that we wish on her behalf in consultation and in concert with the Prosecution to have those three days set aside.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, Mr. O'Sullivan, of course it's -- but it's not a practice that we want to encourage sentence hearings of that length, and also you will bear in mind that there are other matters before the Tribunal which -- including an ongoing trial for which time has to be found. Could I make the point to you too that much of the matter could be produced in written form. I have in mind statements from witnesses and the like, could be produced to the Tribunal in written form. I would have thought that -- of course there may be other witnesses you want to call, but many -- for instance, if you want to produce character witnesses, they can be produced in written form, and the Tribunal can read what they have to say. Well, we've considered the matter, and given the other pressures on the Trial Chamber for time, what we have in mind is to fix the 16th and the morning of the 17th of December for this hearing. If it's necessary to go on longer, of course we'll consider that. But counsel on both sides should work on the basis that the hearing would last a day and a half. We will meanwhile fix a date for -- or dates, rather, for a timetable for the pleadings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. O'Sullivan, we will fix a date for the various pleadings in the matter. I turn next to the question of provisional release. Mr. O'Sullivan, you applied that provisional release should be continued?

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour. That is our request.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Harmon, do you have any objection to that request?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour, we have no objection to that request.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We'll go into private session to discuss one matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I'm told that the confidentiality order in relation to some of these matters needs to be lifted. Is that right? Help me.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honour. Pursuant to Rule 62 ter (C), the plea agreement is required to be disclosed in open session, and therefore we would request that the seal be lifted on the plea agreement only.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. The position is this: Mrs. Plavsic, we're going to take a wholly exceptional course in your case because these are wholly exceptional circumstances. And for reasons of security, we are going to continue your provisional release. You must appear here for sentence on the days which have been fixed. The fact that we have extended the provisional release is not, of course, to be taken as any indication as to a sentence to be passed. That concludes this hearing. The matter is now adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: adjourned at 3.18 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: [Private session] [Confidentiality partially lifted by order of Chamber]
